{
  "verdict": "runtime",
  "cause": "PROMPT_CACHE_CHANGES_OUTPUT",
  "fix": {"action": "set_param", "target": "cache_prompt", "value": "false"},
  "rationale": "The two requests are byte-identical, but the server evaluated the prompt differently each time. Run 1 reused 1 cached token and evaluated 32 fresh (cache_n=1, prompt_n=32). Run 2 reused 28 cached tokens and evaluated only 5 (cache_n=28, prompt_n=5). Splitting the prompt into different batches sends the GPU math through a different path, so the logits shift slightly, and at temperature 0 that is enough to change the first diverging argmax token. This also explains why every call after the first matches the others: they all hit the same 28-token cache state. The seed is not the cause, because the seed has no effect at temperature 0, and a Q4_0 quant run with identical batching would not explain a mismatch that happens only on the first call. To make the test deterministic, send \"cache_prompt\": false in every request, or warm the cache with one discarded call before comparing replies."
}
